item.title: Do Institutions Really Rule? Acemoglu, Johnson & Robinson's Nobel Thesis vs. Human Capital, Malaria Ecology & the Albouy Data Audit — From the 100-fold global wealth chasm, Nogales, and the 38th parallel through AJR's 2001 settler-mortality 2SLS (7.9x Nigeria-to-Chile multiplier), 2002 Reversal of Fortune, Rodrik's 'Institutions Rule,' and Melissa Dell's gold-standard Peruvian mita spatial RDD (-25% consumption) — cross-examined against Glaeser's Human Capital counter-revolution, Sachs's exogenous Malaria Ecology, East Asia's authoritarian growth paradox, Albouy's explosive 36-of-64 archival audit, and spatial-autocorrelation power math
item.description: Why are citizens of Switzerland or the United States roughly 30 to 100 times richer than citizens of Burundi or the Democratic Republic of the Congo—even across twin towns like Nogales sharing identical sun, soil, and history? This five-act adversarial deep dive places Daron Acemoglu, Simon Johnson, and James A. Robinson's 2024 Nobel-winning institutional thesis on full courtroom trial. Walk through the foundational fortress—Colonial Origins (2001), Reversal of Fortune (2002), Rodrik, Subramanian & Trebbi's 'Institutions Rule' (2004), and Melissa Dell's landmark Econometrica spatial discontinuity across Peru's colonial mining mita (-25% consumption and +6 percentage points child stunting two centuries after abolition)—before unleashing the sharpest counter-evidence in political economy. Pause twice to compute the exact 2SLS Wald multiplier (7.9x from Nigeria to Chile), exclusion-restriction bias magnification, and Fieller weak-instrument infinity threshold (F < 3.84) exposed by David Albouy's 2012 archival audit of 36 imputed observations—and engineer a clustered spatial RDD power calculation (340 villages) correcting Morgan Kelly's 3x spatial-autocorrelation t-statistic mirage. Weigh Edward Glaeser and Andrei Shleifer's Human Capital rebuttal, Jeffrey Sachs's exogenous Anopheles Malaria Ecology, and East Asia's authoritarian growth miracles—closing with a de-bundled tri-mechanism protocol and a field guide to spotting hidden institutional-vs-geography battles inside everyday economics papers.

item.title: Marcus Aurelius & Lee Kuan Yew (121–180 CE / 1923–2015) — The Antonine Plague Notebook & the 1965 Separation Tears: Two Reluctant Stewards of Asymmetric Survival
item.description: Pairs Roman philosopher-emperor Marcus Aurelius (121–180 CE) with modern Singapore's founding architect Lee Kuan Yew (1923–2015) across eighteen centuries to dissect Stoic self-command against unsentimental institutional state-building under sudden existential shock. Follows teenage Marcus sleeping on bare boards and waiting twenty-three quiet years under Antoninus Pius before facing the devastating Antonine Plague, Galen's eyewitness medical crisis, the frozen Marcomannic Wars, his two-month Trajan's Forum palace-treasure auction, burning Avidius Cassius's treasonous letters unread, writing private Greek reminders by tent lamp at Carnuntum, and confronting the dynastic trap of Commodus; then traces young Harry Lee dodging the 1942 Japanese Sook Ching massacre queue, taking a Cambridge double-first, riding and breaking the pro-communist union tiger, weeping on live television during Singapore's sudden August 9, 1965 expulsion, absorbing Britain's East-of-Suez pullout, and building Singapore's four-pillar survival engine (English-first MNC leapfrogging, CPIB anti-corruption and benchmarked pay, HDB/CPF mass homeownership with ethnic quotas, and Israeli-advised military deterrence) alongside a candid quantitative audit of both fifty-year compounding growth (USD 516 to USD 55,647 per capita) and its steep civil-liberty cost before Lee's rare 1990 voluntary step-down.
